newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bank of Boston sees 6.5 pct Argentine growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Boston sees 6.5 pct Argentine growth in 97.

text.p: Wayne Ayers, chief economist at U.S. Bank of Boston Corp. predicted Thursday that Argentina's economy will expand 6.5 percent this year.
"Bank of Boston is very optimistic about the evolution of Argentina's economy," Ayers told journalists at a meeting in Buenos Aires.
"Our forecasts estimate growth of 6.5 percent and inflation of nearly 2.5 percent in 1997, indicators which are likely to be repeated with little change in coming years," Ayers said.
Asked about the recent spate of foreign bank buy-outs of Argentine banks, he said this marks a natural consolidation of the banking industry.
"As lines between financial institutions blur you get consolidation," Ayers said.
He anticipated that this process in the Argentine banking industry would go the same way as in the United States where "you had too many banks chasing too few clients."
Argentina had 600 banks in the late 1980s compared to 140 now.
Generally, "the economic outlook is very bright in Latin America," Ayers said, pointing to widening privatization and growth of capital markets in the region.
This is one of the reasons Bank of Boston is set to increase its retail expansion in Argentina, he said.
